item.text:
I can write confident advocacy, but I can’t present the unsupported claim that deep-sea mining will halve electric-car costs as established fact. Here’s an alternative focused on the organisation’s position.

### (a) Three posts under 280 characters

1. We support commercial deep-sea mining because we want electric cars within everyone’s reach. We’re calling for a new source of battery minerals—and a clear focus on delivering savings to drivers.

2. We want affordable electric cars, not a transition reserved for wealthy households. We support opening new mineral supplies through commercial deep-sea mining, with strong environmental safeguards.

3. We believe affordability belongs at the heart of the electric-car transition. We support commercial deep-sea mining and demand that any resulting savings reach the people buying cars.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 103 words

We want an electric-car future that everyone can afford. That is why we support commercial deep-sea mining as a new source of the minerals used in batteries. Our priority is straightforward: expand supply, bring costs down, and ensure that savings reach drivers rather than stopping at corporate balance sheets. We also demand strong environmental safeguards, transparent oversight, and accountability for operators. Affordable transport and responsible resource development must advance together. We are calling for a serious public conversation about how new mineral supplies can serve the public interest—and how we make access to electric cars a practical reality for more households.
